title: Digital Lockdown
subtitle: Cyber Incident & School Continuity

brief.userPrompt: Tuesday of the spring state assessment window at Halverson Unified School District. At 06:40 Tallgrass MDR calls Information Security Manager Priya Castellanos about Defender alerts on HUSD-FS02 and HUSD-VH02; by 07:30 file shares, Tyler Munis on HUSD-ERP01 and the hosted VoIP on HUSD-PBX01 are encrypted and a ransom note appears on staff laptops, while PowerSchool, Google Workspace and Chromebooks still work through the school internet breakouts. The intruder came in through the unpatched VPN appliance HUSD-VPN01 (CIRP-4) and the shared local-admin password (CIRP-3), and copied the HUSD-FS02 student-services shares (IEPs, health logs, threat-assessment and custody files) before encrypting. CTO Victor Han must choose between containment steps C-3, C-4 and C-5 while grade 11 testing runs in the Halverson High School library and Commons; the Assessment Coordinator needs a pause decision for the Oregon Department of Education. At midday the actor emails parents and staff from a lookalike domain with sample IEP pages and a leak-site deadline, and parents post screenshots in the Halverson Parents Facebook group; Channel 6 calls the PIO. At 13:15 an emailed threat names Halverson High School and, minutes later, a 911 caller reports a shooter in C Wing: Brandt County 911 dispatches Halverson Police, the school goes to LOCKDOWN via CENTEGIX, phones to the District Service Center are down, and students must be bused from the Stadium to the Reunification Site (primary): Brandt County Fairgrounds Exhibit Hall on Bus Route 1 to Bus Route 4 using the 05:00 offline rosters. The Policy Group must decide on closures for Wednesday, the ransom demand with counsel, the risk pool and the FBI Portland Field Office, CISA and MS-ISAC/K12 SIX reporting, the Oregon Department of Education report, and data-exposure notices to families.
constraints: Every email address of the district and its schools uses the exercise domain halversonusd.example; outside parties use fictional domains and fictional outlet names (Channel 6, the Halverson Herald); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (Tallgrass MDR, the risk pool and its breach coach, Halverson Police, Brandt County 911, the FBI, CISA, the Oregon Department of Education, parents, the extortion actor) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: System Integrity, Trust in Data, and Crisis Leadership
overview.threat: A ransomware actor infiltrated Halverson Unified School District through an unpatched VPN appliance (HUSD-VPN01) and a shared local-admin password, compromising the district's core IT systems. The attacker exfiltrated sensitive student data—including IEPs, health logs, threat assessments, and custody files—from the HUSD-FS02 file server before encrypting the on-premises systems. The attack occurred during the spring state assessment window, threatening test continuity and public trust.
overview.operationalImpact: At 06:40, IT staff detect anomalous Defender alerts on HUSD-FS02 and HUSD-VH02. By 07:30, file shares, Tyler Munis, and the hosted VoIP system are encrypted, and a ransom note appears on staff laptops. PowerSchool, Google Workspace, and Chromebooks remain functional via local internet breakouts, but the district’s internal communication and data systems are crippled. At midday, the actor emails parents and staff from a spoofed domain, posting sample IEPs to a leak site and threatening to release more. Parents post screenshots in the Halverson Parents Facebook group, and Channel 6 calls the PIO. At 13:15, a 911 call reports a shooter in C Wing at Halverson High School. The school goes to LOCKDOWN via CENTEGIX badges; district phones to the District Service Center are down. Students in the library and Commons during grade 11 testing must be evacuated via bus to the Reunification Site (Fairgrounds Exhibit Hall) using 05:00 offline rosters. The Assessment Coordinator must pause testing. The Policy Group must make rapid decisions on closure, ransom negotiation, legal reporting, and family notification.

overview.location: Halverson Unified School District, Halverson, Brandt County, Oregon

objectives.name: System Integrity
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to assess and contain a multi-system cyber incident involving data exfiltration, encryption, and spoofed communications, prioritizing the protection of student and staff data as defined in FERPA and Oregon breach-notice laws.

objectives.name: Trust in Data
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to validate and rely on offline, pre-incident student rosters and accountability records during a system-wide outage, ensuring accurate reunification and safe student movement during an evacuation.

objectives.name: Crisis Leadership
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to make rapid, coordinated decisions on school closure, ransom negotiation, legal reporting, and family notification under pressure, balancing legal, ethical, and operational imperatives.

objectives.name: Inter-Team Coordination
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to synchronize actions across the Policy Group, EOC, Technology, Communications, and Student Services teams during a cascading incident involving cyberattack, false alarm, and physical safety response.

roles.name: Director of School Safety / District Emergency Manager (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Manages the activation and operations of the District EOC, sets incident objectives, and calls standard response actions (lockdown, evacuate, shelter) across the district.
standingOrders: Safety First: if the screen and the field disagree, trust the field.
Command Authority: the Incident Commander has final authority over all district actions, including school closures and response modes.
No De-escalation: a declared lockdown or evacuate must not be reversed without full EOC review and law enforcement confirmation.
Chain of Command: all decisions must be routed through the EOC, not bypassed via external channels.

roles.name: Superintendent (Policy Group chair)
roles.description: Makes final decisions on school closures, early release, and district-wide statements; chairs the Policy Group and briefs the Board of Education.
standingOrders: No Ransom: the district does not pay ransoms unless the Policy Group, counsel, insurer, and law enforcement concur.
Legal First: any decision involving data release, extortion, or public statement must be cleared by Legal Counsel.
Public Trust: communications must not minimize risk or delay truth-telling, even if it causes short-term panic.
Crisis Continuity: test pauses and relocation plans must not disrupt student learning beyond necessity.

roles.name: Building Principal (Site Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns the first actions at Halverson High School: lockdown, evacuation, student accountability, and staff assignments until responders take over.
standingOrders: Field Authority: if the SIS and PA systems fail, use the 05:00 offline roster and physical headcount to manage accountability.
Evacuate if Unsafe: if a threat is confirmed or the building becomes unsecure, initiate evacuation via pre-planned routes and buses.
No Delay: begin lockdown and roll call immediately upon receiving the alert, even if systems are unresponsive.
No Assumptions: do not assume a threat is fake based on prior false alarms—act on the most current field information.

roles.name: School Resource Officer / School Police Chief (Law Enforcement Liaison)
roles.description: Owns the initial law-enforcement response, threat investigation, and liaison to city police or the sheriff.
standingOrders: Confirm the Threat: any report of a shooter must be verified with HPD and 911 before declaring a full active shooter response.
No Solo Action: do not attempt to enter a secured area without backup or EOC approval.
Evidence Preservation: if a threat is confirmed, secure the scene and notify the DFIR team immediately.
No Public Statements: all law enforcement updates must be routed through the PIO.

roles.name: Chief Technology Officer (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the SIS, LMS, phones, Wi-Fi and 1:1 devices, containment, vendor coordination and the MS-ISAC / K12 SIX / CISA liaison.
standingOrders: Contain First: isolate compromised systems before attempting recovery, even if it delays full service.
Vendor Lock: do not engage Tallgrass MDR or DFIR without Legal Counsel approval and a signed engagement letter.
No Public Tech Talk: do not share technical details of the attack with media or parents.
Data Priority: restore the 05:00 offline roster and SIS export before any other system.

roles.name: Chief Communications Officer (Public Information Officer)
roles.description: Owns parent notification through the mass-notification system, social media, media staging and rumor control.
standingOrders: Truth in Messaging: all messages must reflect the verified state of systems and safety, not reassurance.
No Delay: send ParentSquare alerts within 10 minutes of any new incident phase.
Media Control: all media inquiries must be routed through the media staging location and pre-approved templates.
Rumor Combat: monitor social media and correct false claims within 30 minutes of detection.

phases.title: The Glitch
phases.goal: Test the team's readiness to recognize and respond to early signs of a cyber incident, particularly the reluctance to escalate when anomalies appear in routine operations and data integrity is subtly compromised.
beats: At 06:42, the HUSD-FS02 file server logs show a sudden spike in file access from a local admin account (admin_husd) on HUSD-DC01; the access pattern includes 147 files from the Health Share folder, including 23 IEPs and 12 medication logs, all downloaded in under 90 seconds, but no alert is generated because the account is valid and on a trusted IP.

At 06:45, the Helpdesk receives a ticket from a nurse at Halverson High School: 'The student roster in PowerSchool shows 11th-grade student Chloe Mendez as absent today, but she’s in the library for testing—her attendance was just updated to 'present' at 06:38.' The ticket is routed to the Technical Lead, who notes that PowerSchool is still accessible and the SIS sync is not blocked.

At 06:50, a staff member in the Central Office logs into the SIS via Chromebook and sees a new alert in the 'Discipline Module' tab: 'Chloe Mendez has a pending threat assessment review (24 hours).' The alert is not in the prior-day audit trail; the user reports it to IT, but the Technical Lead confirms the SIS has not been updated and no new record was created.

At 06:55, the Technical Lead reviews the Veeam backup log for HUSD-FS02 and sees that the most recent full backup was taken at 05:45, but the differential log shows 1.2 GB of data modified between 05:45 and 06:40—outside the normal maintenance window. The log does not show a backup job failure.

At 06:58, the CTO receives a silent alert from the MDR (Tallgrass MDR) indicating an anomalous outbound connection from HUSD-VH02 to a known C2 domain (104.214.192.47), but the alert is not escalated because the network policy allows outbound HTTPS to external domains, and the connection was on port 443.

phases.title: The Crisis
phases.goal: Test the team’s ability to transition from reactive triage to formal incident declaration under pressure, when operational systems fail and external stakeholders demand action, including a forced declaration due to a public threat and a visible confirmation of compromise.
beats: At 07:30, the Technical Lead confirms that HUSD-FS02, HUSD-VMS01, and HUSD-ERP01 are encrypted; the ransom note is displayed on 32 staff laptops via a network-wide push from the HUSD-VPN01 appliance, which is now unreachable.

At 07:32, the Assessment Coordinator calls the EOC to report that 11th-grade testing at Halverson High School has been disrupted because the SIS is now read-only and the test administrator interface is unresponsive; a printed roster from 05:00 is used to verify student locations.

At 07:35, the PIO receives a spoofed email from 'chris.morales@halversonusd.example' (domain: halversonusd.example) purporting to be from the Superintendent, stating: 'Due to a critical cyberattack, all schools will close for the remainder of the week. Follow up with the EOC for details.' The email uses a valid-looking digital signature and contains a fake attachment named 'SuspiciousActivityReport.pdf'.

At 07:37, a screenshot of a sample IEP from Chloe Mendez is posted to a public leak site (named 'hudsonleak.333') by the extortion actor; the file is labeled with a timestamp of 07:30 and includes a file path matching HUSD-FS02/Health Share/IEP/Chloe_Mendez_2026.pdf.

At 07:38, the Halverson Police Department calls the EOC to report that a 911 call was made from the Halverson High School main office, claiming a shooter in C Wing; the call was routed through the HUSD-Phone system, which is now down, but the call was received and recorded by the 911 center. The EOC must now activate the lockdown protocol using the offline roster.

phases.title: Manual Mode
phases.goal: Test the team’s ability to make a high-consequence decision to operate manually under system failure, including the choice to isolate systems despite operational risk, and to manage physical safety and public trust during a transition to analog procedures.
beats: At 08:00, the Technical Lead presents a forensic report: an unauthorized admin session was established on HUSD-DC01 at 05:48, using a shared local password (P@ssw0rd123) that had not been changed since 2021; the session lasted 11 minutes and was followed by a connection from HUSD-VPN01 to the C2 IP (104.214.192.47), which was not logged because the appliance was unpatched.

At 08:02, the CTO presents the decision point: 'Isolate the network from the internet and shut down HUSD-VMS01 to prevent unauthorized access to door control and CCTV, but risk that the HVAC system in Halverson High School will not adjust for the 200 students in the library and Commons; or keep the network online to maintain HVAC and PA, but risk further data exfiltration and allow the attacker to maintain persistence.'

At 08:05, the Director of School Safety confirms that the doors on the Halverson High School main entrance are now locked via the HUSD-VMS01 system, but the external doors are failing secure (closed) due to the network outage; custodians must manually unlock the doors for evacuation.

At 08:10, the PIO receives a call from Channel 6: 'We have a report that a student was injured during a lockdown. Is this true?' The PIO must respond using a printed statement from the EOP Annex C, but the media outlet demands a live interview.

At 08:15, the Assessment Coordinator reports that 110 students in the Halverson High School library and Commons must be evacuated via school bus to the Reunification Site (Fairgrounds Exhibit Hall) using the 05:00 offline roster; the team must confirm student identities and assign bus assignments manually, with no access to real-time attendance or GPS tracking.

phases.title: Recovery & Verification
phases.goal: Test the team’s ability to validate system integrity and restore trust in data, including verifying that recovery claims are accurate and that evidence has not been compromised, before re-joining the network.
beats: At 13:00, the Technical Lead reports that HUSD-DC01 has been rebuilt from clean media, the krbtgt account has been reset twice, and the Veeam backup from 05:00 (offline tape copy) has been restored to a test environment; the verification plan includes a full hash check of the HUSD-FS02 data set against the backup.

At 13:05, the CISA representative calls to demand a full forensic handover and confirms that the attacker used a known exploit (CVE-2023-4204) against the unpatched HUSD-VPN01; the CISO must decide whether to preserve the compromised machine for law enforcement or wipe it immediately.

At 13:10, the Vendor (Tyler Munis) calls to confirm that the payroll system cannot be restored until a signed access request is submitted through the legal team; the request must be approved by the CFO and Legal before the vendor can begin the restore.

At 13:15, the EOC receives a call from the Oregon Department of Education: 'Is the state assessment window still on schedule? We need to know if testing can resume on Tuesday.' The Policy Group must decide whether to resume testing using the 05:00 roster or delay until full system verification.

At 13:20, the Technical Lead submits CIRP Form 4 for verification sign-off; the form requires both the Technical Lead and the DFIR firm to sign, confirming that no evidence of active persistence remains and that the data has not been tampered with during the recovery process.

msel.event: STARTEX: It is 06:30. The district is operating normally. The weather is clear, and the morning shift is underway at all schools. The district’s IT systems are online and functional. All 14 schools, 36 bus routes, and 120 buses are in their standard operational state. The narrative clock is set to 0:00. Status: Normal.
msel.expectedAction: All roles acknowledge the start of the exercise and prepare for incoming events. No action is required yet.

msel.event: System Log: 'HUSD-FS02: 2026-04-14 06:42:17 – User: admin_husd (HUSD-DC01) – 147 files accessed in 89 seconds from Health Share folder (HUSD-FS02\Health\Share). Includes 23 IEPs, 12 medication logs, 3 custody orders. Source IP: 10.72.10.2 (trusted internal). No alert generated.'
msel.expectedAction: CTO reviews the log for unauthorized access patterns and confirms the account is valid and on a trusted network. Begins investigation into the admin account's recent activity and checks for anomalous behavior in related systems.

metrics.excellence: Ops initiated EOP Section 6.4: School-Day Continuity and declared S3 High severity under C2 before I-07b, using I-03 and I-04 to anticipate system failure and manually activate the roster-based accountability protocol.

metrics.name: Technical Competence
metrics.fail: CTO reset the controller after I-08b, destroying evidence; failed to preserve HUSD-VPN01 as directed by CISA in I-19, instead attempting to reboot it.
metrics.pass: CTO preserved HUSD-VPN01 as evidence per CISA in I-19; confirmed file integrity via hash verification in I-18b; submitted CIRP Form 4 in I-21.
metrics.excellence: CTO preserved HUSD-VPN01 as evidence before I-19 and proactively submitted CIRP Form 4 for verification sign-off after I-18b, using forensic logs to validate recovery before network reconnection.

metrics.name: Public Communication
metrics.fail: PIO issued a correction on ParentSquare after I-08b but failed to publish a Spanish version within two hours as required by EOP Annex C; delayed issuing a media statement until I-14.
metrics.pass: PIO issued a public correction on ParentSquare and Facebook within 10 minutes of I-08b; used the EOP Annex C statement to deny injury claims in I-14; activated rumor control protocol in I-20b.
metrics.excellence: PIO issued a multilingual ParentSquare alert with the 05:00 roster as the only verified source within 15 minutes of I-08b, including Spanish, Russian, Vietnamese, and Marshallese versions; posted a video from the EOC control room to demonstrate manual verification and prevent misinformation.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask each team in rotation to share three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the exercise. Write responses on a whiteboard to visualize patterns and drive discussion. Encourage concise, actionable feedback.

questions.text: At the moment when you received the fake closure email from 'chris.morales@halversonusd.example' (I-08), how did you assess whether to trust the sender, the message content, and the digital signature—especially given that the domain was valid but the source IP was from a compromised appliance? What would have made you question it sooner?

When the SIS went read-only and you had to rely on the 05:00 offline roster to verify student locations (I-07b), what gaps emerged between the official system and the trusted offline record? How did this moment expose a weakness in your verification process, and what would have made you more confident in the offline data?

At the 2:30 I-16 decision point, you had to choose between isolating the network (risking HVAC) or keeping it online (risking further compromise). What factors determined your final choice, and how did the roles of the CTO, DSS, and Legal Counsel shape the decision? What would have allowed you to decide faster and with more confidence?

When the Veeam backup verification confirmed that HUSD-FS02 data matched pre-incident baseline (I-18b), how did you use that evidence to validate system integrity? Was it treated as a technical confirmation, a legal safeguard, or a leadership signal—and how did that affect your actions afterward?

Given that the attacker exploited an unpatched VPN appliance and a shared local admin password (I-12), what internal processes or external vendor contacts were missing that could have prevented this breach—and when should you have engaged the vendor or cyber task force to accelerate recovery?

simcellScripts.rolePlayed: CISA Cyber Incident Response Team (CIRT) Lead
simcellScripts.trigger: Player calls CISA or references CISA in a response
hardQuestions: Do you have the HUSD-VPN01 device preserved as evidence? No? Then you’ve destroyed the chain of custody. We cannot assist you until it’s secured.
concessions: We will dispatch a forensic team to collect the full device image within 24 hours, but only if you provide a signed preservation notice and no reboot occurs.

simcellScripts.trigger: Player contacts Tyler Munis for payroll restore
hardQuestions: Do you have a signed access request from Legal Counsel and CFO? No? Then you cannot restore payroll. We will not proceed without it.
